claims.statement: The recast Energy Performance of Buildings Directive establishes charging and pre-cabling requirements for specified new and renovated buildings.

The same directive requires Member States to remove barriers to private charging-point installation in residential buildings, creating a regulatory tailwind but not a right to commercial site exclusivity.

contrary_evidence: The directive is subject to national transposition and specifically reduces some consent barriers, so a mandate portfolio may be less scarce than assumed.

economics.acquisition_route: Property-administrator associations, electrical contractors, and standardized email ballots to existing communities rather than consumer-by-consumer selling
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Originate 25 sites by year 2 (unvalidated), 250 sites by year 5 (unvalidated), and retain a revenue-share portfolio supporting founder equity above PLN 5 million by year 7 (unvalidated)
economics.founder_time: 10-16 hours per week during validation (unvalidated), with surveys subcontracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Asset-light site documentation and tendering with engineers paid per survey; 55-70% gross margin (unvalidated)
economics.payback: Portfolio acquisition payback after the first commissioned site within 8-14 months (unvalidated)
economics.pricing: PLN 12000-30000 origination fee per commissioned site (unvalidated) plus a 2-5% operating-revenue share (unvalidated)
economics.retention_or_repeat: Site mandates last 18-30 months (unvalidated); operating revenue shares can recur for 5-8 years (unvalidated)

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: More mandates create geographic density, operator bargaining power, reusable resolution templates, and conversion data
fingerprint.customer: Housing communities, office and retail landlords, and charge-point operators
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Owner-approved site portfolio, feasibility evidence, and competitive operator tender for origination and revenue-share fees
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Charge-point operator pays when a mandate converts into a commissioned site; landlord may pay for an independent feasibility package
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Residents or tenants request charging, or a building renovation exposes parking-electrical work

founder_fit: Builds on renewable-installation and quoting knowledge.
Uses structured feasibility scoring and standardized documents.
Channel partners carry most recurring social interaction.
risks: Grid upgrades can destroy site economics.
The stated PLN 60000 startup capital requirement is unvalidated.

structure.commercial_archetype: Site-rights aggregation and infrastructure project origination
structure.control_point: Exclusive tender and representation mandate over a documented parking-site portfolio
structure.critical_dependency: Valid property resolutions, grid feasibility, and charge-point-operator appetite for the bundled sites

thesis: Obtain time-limited, conditional exclusivity mandates from housing communities and small commercial landlords to survey parking, aggregate electricity demand, and run charger tenders; package many consented sites for licensed charge-point operators instead of financing chargers. The scarce asset is a portfolio of owner-approved, technically documented sites.
title: ChargeMandate Building Portfolio
uncertainties: Which administrator segment can approve mandates with the least delay?
What minimum site bundle changes operator pricing?
